cards.text: Friend, God's people are split into two kingdoms, Judah and Israel (1 Kings 12:19-20). Asa is king of Judah, and in his second year, Nadab son of Jeroboam becomes king of Israel. His dad Jeroboam was the first king of this kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 12:20).

cards.question: Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel for ___ years.

cards.text: TWO years? Friend, I've had oven mitts longer than that. And remember, his dad Jeroboam made two golden calves and set them up in Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-29).

cards.question: True or false: King Nadab breaks from his father Jeroboam's sin and does what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Nadab and all Israel are laying siege to Gibbethon, a city of the Philistines. And in the picture is a man named Baasha, from the house of Issachar.

cards.question: While Israel besieges Gibbethon, what does Baasha do to King Nadab?

answers.text: He kills Nadab and reigns in his place
He fights bravely at Nadab's side
He warns Nadab of a Philistine trap

cards.text: And Baasha doesn't stop with Nadab. As soon as he becomes king, he goes after the entire household of Jeroboam.

cards.question: When King Baasha strikes down Jeroboam's household, how many of them does he leave alive?
Baasha's purge of Jeroboam's house happens according to a word the LORD had spoken earlier. Through which prophet?
Jeroboam's house falls because of the sins Jeroboam committed and caused ___ to commit.

cards.text: Now Baasha is king of all Israel, reigning from the city of Tirzah. And he and Asa of Judah are at war throughout their days.

cards.question: True or false: King Baasha reigns over Israel from Tirzah for twenty-four years.
Jeroboam's house just fell because of Jeroboam's sins. So whose way does the new king Baasha walk in?

cards.text: Jeroboam's house falls for its sins, and the new king walks right into the SAME sin? Friend, that's like taking over for the guy who kept hitting snooze, then sleeping through your first day.
Then the word of the LORD comes to a prophet, Jehu son of Hanani, with a message against King Baasha.

cards.question: In His message through Jehu, God reminds Baasha what He did for him. What was it?

answers.text: Lifted him out of the dust and made him ruler
Gave him victory over the Philistine cities
Saved him from the army of King Asa

cards.text: And still, God says, Baasha walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused Israel to sin. Friend, I spent YEARS in the dust of a junk drawer, and when somebody lifts you out of the dust, you do NOT go roll back in it!

cards.question: God says He will consume Baasha and his house, and make his house like the house of ___.

cards.text: Then a hard word: anyone of Baasha's who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field by the birds of the air. Jeroboam's house got nearly the same warning (1 Kings 14:11).
The rest of Baasha's acts, his accomplishments and his might, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

cards.question: Baasha rests with his fathers and is buried in ___, and his son ___ reigns in his place.

cards.text: Then the text comes back to the LORD's word through Jehu against Baasha and his house. The reasons: all the evil Baasha did, becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and one more you might not see coming.

cards.question: True or false: One reason the LORD's word came against Baasha's house is that Baasha struck down the house of Jeroboam.

cards.text: Baasha's son Elah becomes king and reigns in Tirzah two years. And there he is in Tirzah, getting drunk at the house of Arza, the steward of his household.

cards.question: While King Elah is getting drunk at Arza's house, who conspires against him?

answers.text: Zimri commander of half his chariots
Arza the steward of his household

cards.text: Zimri goes in, strikes Elah down and reigns in his place. Friend, that's like zoning out at the office party while your coworker is measuring your office for curtains.

cards.question: Once Zimri is seated on the throne, what does he do to Baasha's household?

answers.text: He sends them away to Judah
He gives them places at court

cards.question: Zimri destroys Baasha's household according to the word the LORD spoke against Baasha through ___ the prophet.
True or false: The text says Baasha's household falls because of Baasha's sins alone, not his son Elah's.

cards.text: Elah's acts go into the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel too. That's four kings and two wiped-out royal families already, friend, and Israel's throne is a revolving door that is SPINNING.
It's the twenty-seventh year of Asa's reign over Judah, and Zimri now sits on Israel's throne in Tirzah. Don't get too comfortable with this one, friend.

cards.question: Zimri reigns in Tirzah for ___ days.

cards.text: SEVEN DAYS, friend, that's not a reign, that's a free trial! Meanwhile Israel's troops are camped against Gibbethon of the Philistines, and word reaches the camp that Zimri conspired against the king and struck him down.

cards.question: When the troops at Gibbethon hear what Zimri did, what do they do there in the camp that very day?

answers.text: Proclaim Omri the army commander king
Swear their loyalty to King Zimri
Go home to their own tribes

cards.text: Omri and all the Israelites march up from Gibbethon and besiege Tirzah, where Zimri is.

cards.question: When Zimri sees that Tirzah is captured, what does he do?

answers.text: Burns the palace citadel down on himself
Flees south to King Asa in Judah
Surrenders the city to Omri's army

cards.question: Zimri dies because of his sins, following the example of ___ and the sin he caused Israel to commit.

cards.text: Zimri's treason gets written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Now the people are split right down the middle: half back Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half back Omri.

cards.question: Israel is split between Tibni and Omri. How does it end?

answers.text: Omri's side wins and he becomes king
Tibni and Omri share the throne
Tibni's side wins and Omri flees

cards.text: In the thirty-first year of Asa's reign, Omri becomes king of Israel and reigns twelve years, six of them in Tirzah. He buys a hill from a man named Shemer for two talents of silver and builds a city there.

cards.question: Omri names his new city ___ after Shemer, who had owned the hill.

cards.text: Omri names his city after the guy who sold him the hill. Friend, that's like buying a used car and naming it Gary, because Gary sold it to you.

cards.question: Omri has a brand new capital. True or false: Omri acts more wickedly in the sight of the LORD than all who were before him.

cards.text: Omri walks in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, provoking the LORD with worthless idols. Then he rests with his fathers, is buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigns in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Asa's reign over Judah, Omri's son Ahab becomes king of Israel. He reigns in Samaria twenty-two years, so friend, this one is NOT a free trial.

cards.question: How does King Ahab do in the sight of the LORD compared to all who were before him?

answers.text: He does more evil than all of them
He does better than his father did
He does right like King Asa did

cards.text: And as if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam, Ahab marries Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians.

cards.question: After marrying Jezebel, who does Ahab go on to serve and worship?
Ahab sets up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal he built in ___.
After the altar for Baal, what does Ahab set up next?

cards.text: So Ahab does more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him. Friend, his dad set the bar, and Ahab basically said, hold my apron.
One more thing happens in Ahab's days: Hiel from Bethel rebuilds Jericho. Long before, the LORD had spoken a word through Joshua son of Nun about whoever would rebuild that city (Joshua 6:26).

cards.question: What does rebuilding Jericho cost Hiel?

answers.text: His firstborn son and his youngest son
All the silver and gold he owned
His house and his fields in Bethel

cards.question: True or false: What happens to Hiel's sons is according to the word the LORD spoke through Joshua son of Nun.

cards.text: Kings come and go in this passage, friend, one for two years, one for seven days. But the word of the LORD? It didn't budge one crumb.

findings.problem: The walkthrough uses 4 stops of 14, 16, 14 and 11 cards. The 55 cards would fit in 3 stops of about 18, so the fourth stop is an extra break the passage doesn't need.

rule.text: About 1 to 3 stops per passage. No hard cap. Use whatever fits the passage, but never let it run long.

findings.problem: Nothing on card 1 lets the baker reason out how long Nadab reigned (two, twenty or forty years). The pick is pure luck, and the reign length is a small detail that doesn't move the passage.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The setup says Baasha 'goes after the entire household of Jeroboam'. That rules out the wrong answers on card 8 ('Only the women and children', 'Only Jeroboam's youngest son') and gives away how many he left alive.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The repeated line 'which he had caused Israel to commit' first appears in 15:26, which card 4 already covered. Card 10 asks about it again at 15:30.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Card 11 gives nothing that would let the baker judge whether Baasha reigned twenty-four years. The true or false is a coin flip on a number.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'Walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin' (15:34) repeats the line from 15:26, which card 4 already asked about.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Lifted him out of the dust and made him ruler', is poetic Bible wording and is longer than the others. The two wrong answers are plain modern phrasing, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'Following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit' (16:19) is the same repeated line, already asked about in stop 1. The question and its wrong answers (David, Asa) are almost identical to stop 2 card 4.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The setup already says the LORD spoke a word through Joshua son of Nun about whoever would rebuild Jericho. That gives away card 10's true or false, which asks whether what happens to Hiel's sons is according to the word the LORD spoke through Joshua.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card tells nothing new from 16:34. It recaps the reign lengths and sums up the passage, even though it cites 16:34.

rule.text: No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage.
